title: Freshness and Recrawl: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Freshness and Recrawl: Visual Guide

1. Frontier Meets Freshness | five pages of different classes ordered either by age (the plain crawl frontier) or by w(1-e^(-lambda*a))/c, with a fetch-budget slider and the expected changes each policy finds | the queue machinery from the earlier lessons was already right, but age alone is not staleness risk - the expected value of a fetch is, and politeness plus a maximum audit interval still gate whatever ordering wins

2. The Change Curve | an SVG plot of P(changed by t) = 1 - e^(-lambda*t) with five page-class presets (release notes 0.5/day down to a policy PDF at 1/365) and a days-since-verified slider | the curve is concave with its coin-flip point at ln2/lambda, so release notes hit 0.393 in a day and 0.865 in four while a policy PDF reaches only 1.9% in a whole week - one weekly schedule is wrong for both

3. Counting From History | steppers for c changes over T observed days, a prior switch, and a polling-interval slider showing the censored estimator (1-e^(-lambda*k))/k against a true 0.5/day page | the raw c/T estimate needs Gamma smoothing to (alpha+c)/(beta+T) when history is sparse, and slow polling systematically undercounts fast pages because three changes between checks are observed as one

4. Priority Per Fetch | four sliders (importance, change rate, age, fetch cost) driving page A against a fixed page B, with both priority bars and the formula spelled out under each | priority is expected value per unit of cost, so cost is a divisor and not a tiebreak - A's 2.26 falls to 0.226 at cost 10 and loses to B's 0.39 - and the numerator saturates, which is why every page needs an audit deadline

5. Recency Meets Relevance | three query-intent presets for alpha, a half-life slider driving r(a) = 2^(-a/h), and a toggle between decaying the content date and decaying crawl time, scoring an old canonical document against a recent one | recency is fused with relevance rather than replacing it, so it flips a result only when alpha is large enough to close the 0.15 relevance gap - and decaying crawl time instead of a content date makes a freshly refetched ancient document look new
